//: DELIBERATELY NO `firestore.rules` KEY. It used to point at firestore.rules -- the PERMISSIVE EMULATOR ruleset (`allow read, write: if true`) -- so a bare `firebase deploy`, or `--only firestore`, would have deployed a WIDE OPEN database to production. Production rules are authored and deployed through the Firebase console; the review copy is firestore.rules.prod. Removing the key makes that mistake impossible: deploy can no longer touch Firestore rules at all.
//2: EXPECTED SIDE EFFECT, verified not assumed: the emulator now prints `Did not find a Cloud Firestore rules file` on every start and defaults to allowing all reads and writes. That is the SAME effective behaviour as before, because the file it used to load was itself `allow read, write: if true` -- the warning is noise, not a regression. firestore.rules is kept in the repo as documentation of dev intent, and because restoring the key is the way to make the emulator enforce rules if that is ever wanted.
//3: To test rules against the emulator WITHOUT this key, load a ruleset per scratch project id: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8080/emulator/v1/projects/{projectId}:securityRules. That is how firestore.rules.prod was verified, and it leaves real sample data untouched.
